title: Exploring the Dynamic Interplay of Deleterious Variants on the RAF1-RAP1A Binding in Cancer: Conformational Analysis, Binding Free Energy, and Essential Dynamics.
authors: Khan, Abbas; Ali, Syed Shujait; Zahid, Muhammad Ammar; Abdelsalam, Shahenda Salah; Albekairi, Noorah; Al-Zoubi, Raed M; Shkoor, Mohanad; Wei, Dong-Qing; Agouni, Abdelali
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习筛选和全原子MD模拟研究RAF1-RAP1A蛋白-蛋白互作中致病突变对结合亲和力的影响，虽非TF-DNA体系，但蛋白互作建模与MD方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: The RAF1-RAP1A interaction activates the MAPK/ERK pathway which is very crucial in the carcinogenesis process. This protein complex influences tumor formation, proliferation, and metastasis. Understanding aberrant interactions driven by clinical mutations is vital for targeted therapies. Hence, the current study focuses on the screening of clinically reported substitutions in the RAF1 and RAP1A genes using predictive algorithms integrated with all-atoms simulation, essential dynamics, and binding free energy methods. Survival analysis results revealed a strong association between RAF1 and RAP1A expression levels and diminished survival rates in cancer patients across different cancer types. Integrated machine learning algorithms showed that among the 134 mutations reported for these 2 proteins, only 13 and 35 were classified as deleterious mutations in RAF1 and RAP1P, respectively. Moreover, one mutation in RAF1 reported elevated levels of binding between RAF1 and RAP1P while in RAP1A, 7 mutations were reported to increase the binding affinity. The high-binding mutations, P34Q and V60F, were subjected to protein-protein coupling which confirmed the increase in the binding affinity. Wild-type and mutant RAF1-RAP1P bound complexes were subjected to molecular simulation investigation, revealing enhanced structural stability, increased compactness, and stabilized residue fluctuations of the mutant systems in contrast to the wild-type. In addition, hydrogen bonding analysis revealed a variation in the binding paradigm which further underscores the impact of these substitutions on the coupling of RAF1 and RAP1A. Principal component analysis (PCA) and free energy landscape (FEL) evaluation further determined dynamical variations in the wild-type and mutant complexes. Finally, the Gibbs free energy for each complex was estimated and found to be -71.94 +/- 0.38 kcal/mol for the wild-type, -95.57 +/- 0.37 kcal/mol for the V60F, and -85.76 +/- 0.72 kcal/mol for P34Q complex. These findings confirm the effect of these variants on increasing the binding affinity of RAF1 to RAP1P. These mutations can therefore be targeted for cancer therapy to modulate the activity of the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: RAF1-RAP1A相互作用激活MAPK/ERK通路，该通路在癌变过程中至关重要。该蛋白复合物影响肿瘤形成、增殖和转移。理解由临床突变驱动的异常相互作用对于靶向治疗至关重要。因此，本研究聚焦于利用预测算法结合全原子模拟、本质动力学和结合自由能方法，筛选RAF1和RAP1A基因中临床报告的替换突变。生存分析结果显示，RAF1和RAP1A表达水平与不同癌症类型患者生存率降低之间存在强关联。集成机器学习算法表明，在这两种蛋白报告的134个突变中，分别只有13个和35个被分类为RAF1和RAP1P中的有害突变。此外，RAF1中的一个突变被报告提高了RAF1与RAP1P之间的结合水平，而在RAP1A中，有7个突变被报告增加了结合亲和力。高结合突变P34Q和V60F经过蛋白-蛋白偶联分析，确认了结合亲和力的增加。野生型和突变型RAF1-RAP1P结合复合物经过分子模拟研究，揭示了突变系统相较于野生型具有增强的结构稳定性、增加的紧凑性和稳定的残基波动。此外，氢键分析揭示了结合模式的变异，进一步强调了这些替换对RAF1和RAP1A偶联的影响。主成分分析（PCA）和自由能景观（FEL）评估进一步确定了野生型和突变型复合物中的动力学变异。最后，估计了每个复合物的吉布斯自由能，发现野生型为-71.94 +/- 0.38 kcal/mol，V60F为-95.57 +/- 0.37 kcal/mol，P34Q复合物为-85.76 +/- 0.72 kcal/mol。这些发现证实了这些变异对增加RAF1与RAP1P结合亲和力的影响。因此，这些突变可作为癌症治疗的靶点，以调节MAPK/ERK信号通路的活性。
